rules.requirement: Accept a human idea from docs/idea.md, any human-named repository file, or the current prompt without requiring a form.
Treat one paragraph, partial notes, blanks, and idk as sufficient planning input.
Ask one to three focused questions at a time, place a recommended option first, and suggest names and overlooked development concerns.
Draft a plain-language product or project destination after the first planning pass.
Keep the active release narrow while retaining lightweight later-release outcomes through the end goal.
Capture functional, quality, interface, data, platform, safety, and failure requirements when applicable.
Map every active-release requirement to a capability block, spike, or explicit deferral before implementation.
Decompose only the current capability block and immediate horizon into executable work items.
Resolve high-risk unknowns with bounded spikes before freezing dependent architecture or backlogs.
Require human approval of product shape, active-release outcomes, major architecture, and the first execution goal before product implementation.
Define each active execution goal with outcome, verification, constraints, boundaries, iteration policy, and blocked stop condition.
Use maturity levels L0 risk, L1 walking skeleton, L2 functional, L3 hardened, and L4 release proven.
Complete a manually exercised end-to-end walking skeleton before exhaustive module hardening.
Reassess the plan after each runtime demonstration, architecture-changing discovery, or block maturity transition.
Map every local requirement in the current block to a work item, spike, or explicit deferral before claiming functional maturity.
Store explicit human evidence for product-shape, major-architecture, and first-goal approval before leaving planning.
Give every mutable fact one canonical owner and generate secondary views where useful.
A routine task should update at most its canonical work item; status changes only for handoff truth.
Keep generated status to at most twenty-five lines and exclude historical evidence narration.
Record durable material choices as decisions and keep unresolved choices in their owning product or block document.
Maintain one concise copy-paste command reference and update setup guides only when setup changes.
Create user, operator, and release guides only when the project has real behavior to document.
Keep domain correctness independent from volatile UI, framework, network, storage, or platform boundaries when the separation removes real risk.
Do not impose ports, adapters, packages, or abstractions without a demonstrated boundary, reuse, testability, or volatility benefit.
Fix root causes and reject broad conditional band-aids, fake success, swallowed errors, and silent contract downgrades.
Fail fast for invalid configuration, impossible state, schema mismatch, and unsupported platform assumptions.
Handle expected external failures with explicit typed, observable, safe, documented, and tested recovery or degradation.
Evaluate mature maintained libraries and repositories before implementing common capabilities, including license, security, maintenance, platform, and integration cost.
Require focused automated validation plus manual inspection where runtime, visual, hardware, operational, or subjective behavior matters.
Activate measurable security, privacy, reliability, observability, migration, rollback, backup, cost, accessibility, and performance gates according to project risk.
Define first-time setup, pinned runtimes, package management, services, secrets, verification, and CI parity before implementation.
Support Linux and Windows development explicitly when both are target environments.
Prefer containers or devcontainers for shared runtimes, services, databases, queues, and CI parity when they reduce cross-platform drift.
Keep native SDKs, simulators, hardware access, signing, installers, and platform-specific packaging on the host when containers reduce reliability.
Validate setup and release commands from a clean supported environment.
Define user flows, product states, errors, permissions, and contracts before final visual implementation while validating them through an early thin interface.
Generate exactly two complete visual directions when direction is unresolved; permit one existing direction when brand or human choice already resolves it.
Use the image generation skill for concept mockups and suitable custom raster assets.
Require exact semantic color, typography, spacing, shape, layout, breakpoint, component, state, asset, motion, and accessibility rules before UI implementation.
Record human selection before implementing the final visual direction.
Translate the selected direction into code-level tokens and an executable component gallery that becomes the exact implementation reference.
Create page, major state, modal, configuration, and responsive references just in time for each active UI block.
Generate distinct shipping raster assets one by one rather than cropping a combined generated sheet.
Prefer maintained icon systems and code-native controls for familiar interface symbols.
Capture matching viewports and important states, compare manually or by visual diff, fix drift, and record approved exceptions.
Use every approved generated shipping asset or explicitly record a human-approved replacement or deferral.
Allow the general template to activate the complete UI workflow without changing template families.
Exercise core behavior headlessly or through the thinnest unstyled real interface before final visual implementation.
Represent tasks, bugs, features, spikes, and gates with one canonical work-item format.
Validate work-item identity, type, status, block, requirements, dependencies, maturity, criteria, and evidence.
Treat a work item as ready only when dependencies and required external inputs are satisfied and validation is known.
Accept human bug reports in any format and let the agent own triage and routing.
Allow an immediate local bug to close through a root-cause fix, regression evidence, and commit without a permanent bug document.
Create bug work items for unresolved, cross-block, recurring, security-sensitive, data-integrity, or release-impacting defects.
Define specific observable success criteria before hardening and require more than passing tests for production completion.
Derive queue, dependency, traceability, block maturity, and release views from canonical work items and release state.
Keep disposable work evidence in a gitignored location.
Retain only release-relevant evidence under a versioned manifest and configurable size budget.
Promote recurring validation into tests or CI and retire task-specific scripts that no longer add a distinct invariant.
Require LFS or external storage policy for retained large binary evidence.
Inspect worktree state, stage only intended files, preserve user changes, and commit coherent validated units.
Use tagged imperative commits with a work-item ID when one exists.
Push at coherent checkpoints when a remote exists, but never update documentation solely to record a successful push.
Record an unpushed-work blocker only when it materially affects handoff.
Keep human.md human-only and never read, summarize, edit, stage, commit, or use it as agent context.
Keep root agent guidance concise and route repeatable procedures to focused progressively disclosed skills.
Publish repository skills to current Codex and Claude discovery locations from one canonical skill source.
Give skills narrow positive and negative trigger boundaries and deterministic scripts where mechanical enforcement matters.
Generate all template repositories from one versioned canonical source plus profiles and capabilities.
Provide deterministic rendering, export drift checks, migrations, changelog, and template provenance.
Run structural, scenario, skill, migration, and large-backlog checks on Linux and Windows.
Prevent removal of a contract rule unless the parity map records explicit human approval.
